edges.effect_quant: Telehealth rehabilitation generally improves or preserves adherence relative to center-based rehabilitation, and the latest network meta-analysis ranked wearable-plus-app models particularly well for adherence-related outcomes.
edges.population: adults with coronary or other cardiovascular disease eligible for cardiac rehabilitation
edges.mechanism: Remote delivery lowers travel and scheduling barriers that often limit center-based rehabilitation completion. When telehealth programs also provide monitoring, feedback, and coaching, they can improve persistence with exercise and lifestyle tasks rather than only replicating in-person sessions digitally.
edges.summary: The best overall read is that tele-cardiac rehabilitation does not just preserve fitness outcomes; it can also help participation and adherence by reducing practical access barriers. The strongest recent synthesis is the 2024 network meta-analysis, and the randomized post-ACS and post-MI trials fit that picture by showing better sustained activity or rehabilitation uptake when remote support is built in.
edges.caveats: Tele-rehabilitation is not automatically superior for every patient or every adherence metric, and many trials are still relatively small. Program design matters: simple remote substitution is less convincing than interventions that combine monitoring, coaching, and behavioral support.
